title: DPOF: Digital Print Order Format

pic_descriptions.description: Small line drawing of a camera or printer connection port with cables or connectors shown nearby, illustrating a DPOF or print-related connection.
Line drawing of a camera connected to a desktop printer, with paper in the printer output tray.

text:
With DPOF (Digital Print Order Format), you can use the camera to specify which images in the CF card are to be printed and the quantity. This feature is very convenient when you make prints with a DPOF-compatible printer or photo lab.

### About DPOF

DPOF (Digital Print Order Format) is a standard for recording print ordering instructions to the CF card. It is for images taken with a digital camera, and you can specify which photos and the quantity to print. With a DPOF-compatible digital camera,
- By inserting a CF card into a DPOF-compatible printer, you can make prints as specified.

Printers capable of direct printing from the camera can print the images as specified by DPOF.

- When ordering prints from a photo lab, you do not need to fill in any order form to specify the image selections, quantity, etc.

text:
### Print settings

Set the print type, date imprinting, and file No. imprinting. The print settings will be applied to all print-ordered images. (They cannot be set individually for each image.)

<PIC:Manual10_223>
{{image description: Print settings table with rows for Print Type, Date, and File No. Print Type options include Standard, Index, and Both; Date and File No. options include On and Off, with descriptions explaining what each setting prints.}}

Select [Print Order].

Turn the dial to select [Print Order], then press <SET>. The Print Order screen will appear. Turn the dial to select [Set up], then press <SET>. The print setting screen will appear. Set the [Print Type], [Date], and [File No.].

Turn the dial to select the menu item, then press <SET>.
Turn the dial to select the desired setting, then press <SET>.

<PIC:Camera_68>
{{image description: Camera menu screen titled Print Order, section Set up. It lists Print Type set to Standard, Date set to Off, and File No. set to Off, with a MENU return icon.}}

<PIC:Manual10_224>
{{image description: Three small Print Order setup screenshots labeled Print Type, Date, and File No., showing menu selection examples for Standard, Index, Both, On, and Off.}}

Exit the menu.

Press the <MENU> button. The Print Order screen will reappear. Next, select [Order] or [All] to select the images to be printed.
- RAW images cannot be selected for printing.


- Even if [Date] and [File No.] are set to [On], the date or file No. might not be imprinted depending on the print type setting and printer type.

- With [Index] prints, both the [Date] and [File No.] cannot be set to [On] at the same time.

- When printing with DPOF, you must use the CF card whose Print Order specifications have been set. It will not work if you just extract images from the CF card and try to print them.

- Certain DPOF-compatible printers and photo labs might not be able to print the photos as you specified. If this happens with your printer, refer to the printer's instruction manual. Or check with your photo lab about compatibility when ordering prints.

- Do not insert into the camera a CF card containing images captured by a different camera and then try to order prints. The print order icon will appear and the images specified for the print order might all be overwritten unintentionally. Also, depending on the image file format, the print order may not be possible.

title: Resetting All Custom Functions
text:
#### C. Fn-02 Long exposure noise reduction

0: Off

1: On

Reduces noise in exposures 1 sec. or longer. After the picture is taken, the time required for noise-reduction processing will be the same as the exposure time. During the noise reduction processing, "busy" will be displayed and shooting will not be possible.

#### C. Fn-03 Flash sync speed in Av mode
0: Auto

1:1/250sec. (fixed)

Sets the flash sync speed to 1/250 sec. in the aperture-priority AE (Av) mode. (Against dark backgrounds such as the night sky, the subject's background will look dark.)

#### C. Fn-04 Shutter button/AE lock button

0: AF/AElock

1: AE lock/AF

Convenient when you want to focus and meter separately. Press the AE lock button to autofocus and press the shutter button halfway to attain AE lock.

2: AF/AF lock, no AE lock

In the AI Servo AF mode, you can press the AE lock button to stop the AF operation momentarily. This prevents the AF from being thrown off by any obstacle passing between the camera and subject. The exposure is set at the moment the picture is taken.

3: AE/AF, no AE lock

This is useful for subjects which keep moving and stopping repeatedly. In the AI Servo AF mode, you can press the AE lock/AF button to start or stop the AI Servo AF operation. The exposure is set at the moment the picture is taken. Thus, the focusing and exposure will always be at the optimum point as you wait for the decisive moment. C. Fn-04 and C. Fn-17-0, 1, 2 (p.146) both have AF start/stop and AE lock functions. If you have set both these Custom Functions and you execute both Custom Function operations, the latter operation will not work. The only exception will be when AF stop is executed after AF start.

text:
#### C. Fn-09 Bracket sequence / Auto cancel

You can change the AEB sequence when the pictures are bracketed with the shutter speed or aperture and the file-saving sequence for white balance bracketing (WB-BKT). When "Auto cancellation" is set, bracketing will be canceled in the following cases: AEB: You turn the switch to <OFF>, change lenses, have flash ready, replace the battery, or replace the CF card. WB-BKT: You turn the switch to <OFF>, replace the battery, or replace the CF card.

| Setting | Sequence | Auto cancel | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0, -, + | Enable | The first bracketed shot is the standard exposure or standard white balance. |
| 1 | 0, -, + | Disable | The first bracketed shot is the standard exposure or standard white balance, and the sequence can be repeated. |
| 2 | -, 0, + | Enable | Starts the bracketing sequence with the minus setting, or the bluish/magenta bias setting for white balance bracketing. |
| 3 | -, 0, + | Disable | Starts the bracketing sequence with the minus setting, or the bluish/magenta bias setting, and the sequence can be repeated. |

#### C. Fn-10 Superimposed display

title: Resetting All Custom Functions
text:
#### C. Fn-13 AF point selection method

0: Normal

Press the AF point selection button and use the Multi-controller to select the AF point.

1: Multi-controller direct

Without pressing the AF point selection button first, you can just use the Multi-controller to select the desired AF point. Pressing the Multi-controller will set it to automatic AF point selection.

2: Quick Control Dial direct

At first, you can just use the Quick Control Dial to select an AF point directly without pressing the AF point selection button. By holding down the AF point selection button and turning the Main Dial, you can set the exposure compensation.

#### C. Fn-14 E-TTL II

0: Evaluative

Fully automatic flash photography for all conditions, from low light to daylight fill-flash.

1: Average

The flash is averaged for the entire area covered by the flash. Since automatic flash exposure compensation will not be executed, you may have to set it yourself depending on the scene. This also applies if you use FE lock.

title: Resetting All Custom Functions
text:
#### C. Fn-15 Shutter curtain sync

0: 1st-curtain sync

1: 2nd-curtain sync

When a slow shutter speed is set, you can capture a light trail following the subject. The flash fires right before the shutter closes. This Custom Function can be used to obtain 2nd-curtain sync effects even with EX-series Speedlites which do not have this feature. If the EX-series Speedlite has this feature, it will override this Custom Function.

When 2nd-curtain sync is used, a preflash will be fired for flash metering control right after you press the shutter button completely. Remember that the main flash will fire right before the shutter closes.

#### C. Fn-16 Safety shift in AV or TV

0: Disable

1: Enable

This works in the shutter-priority AE (Tv) and aperture-priority AE (Av) modes. If the subject's brightness changes suddenly and the current shutter speed or aperture becomes unsuitable, the shutter speed or aperture is shifted automatically to obtain a suitable exposure.

title: Resetting All Custom Functions
text:
#### C. Fn-17 Lens AF stop button function

0: AF stop

1: AF start  AF operates only while the AF stop button is pressed. While the button is pressed, AF operation with the camera is disabled.

2: AE lock while metering

When the button is pressed while metering is still active, AE lock is applied. Convenient when you want to focus and meter separately.

3: AF point: M -> Auto / Auto -> center

In the manual AF point selection mode, holding down the button switches to automatic AF point selection. Holding down the button switches from manual AF point selection to automatic AF point selection instantly. Convenient when you are no longer able to focus track a moving subject with a manually-selected AF point in the AI Servo AF mode. In the automatic AF point selection mode, holding down the button selects the center AF point instantly.

4: ONE SHOT -> AI SERVO

In the One-Shot AF mode, the AF stop button switches to the AI Servo AF mode only while you hold it down. In the AI Servo AF mode, the AF stop button switches to the One-Shot AF mode only while you hold it down. Convenient when you need to keep switching between One-Shot AF and AI Servo AF for a subject which keeps moving and stopping.

5: IS start

With the lens' IS switch already ON, the Image Stabilizer operates only while you press the AF stop button.

The AF stop button is provided only on super telephoto lenses.

#### C. Fn-18 Add original decision data

0: Off

1: On

Data for verifying whether the image is original or not is appended to the image. When an image appended with the verification data is played back, the verification icon will be displayed. (p.104) To verify whether the image is original, the Data Verification Kit DVK-E2 (optional) is required.

title: Power Source
text:
### Power Source

The battery cannot be recharged.
- You are using the wrong battery.

Do not recharge any battery pack other than Battery Pack BP-511A, BP-514, BP-511, or BP-512.

- The battery is not properly attached to the battery charger.
Attach the battery properly to the charger. (p.18)  The camera does not operate even when the power switch is set to <ON>.
- The battery is exhausted.
Recharge the battery. (p.18)
- The battery is not installed properly.
Install the battery properly. (p.20)

- Battery compartment cover is not closed.
Close the battery compartment cover tightly. (p.20)
- CF card slot cover is not closed.
Close the CF card slot cover firmly. (p.24)  The access lamp blinks even when the power switch is set to <OFF>
- If you set the power switch to <OFF> right after shooting, the access lamp will still light/blink for a few seconds while the image is recorded onto the CF card.
When the camera finishes recording the image to the CF card, the access lamp will stop blinking and the power will turn off automatically.  The battery becomes exhausted quickly.
- The battery is not fully charged. Recharge the battery fully. (p.18)
- The battery's service life has expired. Replace the battery with a new one.
The camera turns off by itself.
- Auto power off is in effect. Press the shutter button halfway. If you do not want auto power off to take effect, set [Auto power off] on the menu to [Off]. Only the battery icon blinks on the top LCD panel.
- The battery is almost exhausted. Recharge the battery. (p.18)

title: Troubleshooting: Shooting
text:
### Troubleshooting: Shooting

No images can be shot or recorded.
- The CF card is not properly inserted.

Insert the CF card properly. (p.24)

- The CF card is full.
Use a new CF card or erase unnecessary images. (p.24, 112)

- The battery is exhausted.
Recharge the battery. (p.18)

- You did not focus well. (The focus confirmation light in the viewfinder blinks.)
Press the shutter button halfway again and focus the subject. If you still cannot focus properly, focus manually. (p.26, 70)  The LCD monitor does not display a clear image.
- The LCD monitor screen is dirty.
Use a soft, lens cloth to clean the screen.

- The LCD's service life has expired.
Consult your nearest customer service center or dealer.
**The image is out of focus.**

The lens focus mode switch is set to <MF>.

Set the lens focus mode switch to <AF> (p.23)

- Camera shake occurred when you pressed the shutter button.
To prevent camera shake, hold the camera still and press the shutter button gently. (p.26,38)

**The CF card cannot be used.**
- [Err **] is displayed on the LCD panel.
If it is [Err CF], see page 114.
If it is [Err 02], see page 153.

- You are using a CF card.
Using CF cards is recommended. (p.155)

text:
### Troubleshooting: Image Review and Operation

The image cannot be erased.
- The image is erase-protected. Cancel the protection. (p.111)  The wrong shooting date and time is displayed.
- The correct date and time has not been set. Set the correct date and time. (p.34)  No image appears on the TV screen.
- Video cable plugs are not inserted all the way. Insert the video cable plugs firmly all the way. (p.110)
- The correct video format (NTSC or PAL) has not been set. Set the camera to the correct video format to match the TV set. (p.31)

If a camera error occurs, "Err xx" will be displayed on the LCD panel. Follow the instruction below to resolve the problem for respective error code.
If the same error occurs often, something is probably wrong with the camera. Jot down the "xx" error code and take your camera to the nearest customer service center.
If an error occurs after you take a picture, the camera might have missed the shot. Press the Playback button to see if the image appears on the LCD monitor.

text:
### AC Adapter Kit ACK-E2

Power source kit (AC adapter, DC coupler, power cord) for supplying power to the camera with a household power outlet. Compatible with AC 100 - 240 V.

<PIC:Manual10_237>
{{image description: Product photo of AC Adapter Kit ACK-E2 components, including cables, a coupler-like block, and a power adapter.}}

### Compact Power Adapter CA-PS400

Quick charger for BP-511A. It takes about 110 minutes to recharge one pack. Two packs can be attached to it at one time. DC Coupler DR-400 (optional) can also be connected to the CA-PS400. Compatible with AC 100-240 V.

<PIC:Manual10_238>
{{image description: Product photo of Compact Power Adapter CA-PS400 with a power cord and a black charging unit.}}

### Battery Grip BG-E2

This accommodates two BP-511A packs or six size-AA batteries. It has a vertical-grip shutter button, electronic dial, AE lock/FE lock button, and AF point selection button.

<PIC:Manual10_239>
{{image description: Product photo of a Canon camera body fitted with a Battery Grip BG-E2 on the bottom.}}

### Semi-Hard Case EH17-L

Dedicated case to protect the camera. It can accommodate the camera attached with the EF-S17-85mm f/4-5.6 IS USM lens (optional).

<PIC:Manual10_240>
{{image description: Product photo of a Semi-Hard Case EH17-L, shown as a black fitted camera case.}}

### Shoe-mount Speedlites

An EX-series Speedlite can be attached to the cameras hot shoe. In the same way as normal exposures, you can use E-TTL II autoflash for flash exposures.

<PIC:Manual10_241>
{{image description: Product photo of three shoe-mount Speedlites of different sizes.}}

text:
### Macro Ring Lites

The EX-series Macro Lites (two models) are ideal for close-up flash photography. You can fire only one or both flash tubes and control the flash ratio to easily obtain sophisticated lighting effects with E-TTL II autoflash.

<PIC:Camera_77>
{{image description: Product photo of a macro ring lite system with a circular flash head, coiled cord, and control unit.}}

### Remote Switch RS-80N3

This is a remote switch to prevent camera shake for super-telephoto shots, macro shooting, and bulb exposures. The cord is 80 cm/2.6 ft. The switch provides the same effect as pressing the shutter button halfway or completely. A shutter-release lock is also provided. The connection plug for the camera has a quick-lock feature.

<PIC:Manual10_242>
{{image description: Product photo of Remote Switch RS-80N3 with a hand control, cable, and connector.}}

### Timer Remote Controller TC-80N3

Attached with an 80 cm / 2.6 ft cord, this remote switch has four built-in functions: 1. Self-timer, 2. Interval timer, 3. Bulb-exposure timer, and 4. Shutter-release count setting. The timer can be set anywhere from 1 sec. to 99 hours, 59 min., 59 sec. in 1-sec. increments. The connection plug for the camera has a quick-lock feature.

<PIC:Manual10_243>
{{image description: Product photo of Timer Remote Controller TC-80N3 with a rectangular control body, cable, and connector.}}

### E-series Dioptric Adjustment Lenses

One of ten E-series dioptric adjustment lenses (-4 to +3 diopters) can be attached to the camera's eyepiece to further expand the dioptric adjustment range.

<PIC:Manual10_244>
{{image description: Product photo of an E-series dioptric adjustment lens, shown as a small rectangular eyepiece insert.}}

pic_descriptions.description: A line drawing of a camera lens viewed from the mount side, with the lens electrical contacts highlighted by a dark ring near the rear opening.

Front/top camera body parts diagram with many callouts. Labels include AF/WB button, Drive/ISO button, metering/flash exposure compensation button, main dial, shutter button, self-timer lamp, grip battery compartment, DC coupler cord hole, mirror, contacts, lens mount, EF and EF-S lens mount indexes, hot shoe, mode dial, strap mount, flash button, terminal cover, lens release button, and body cap.

Rear camera body parts diagram with callouts for dioptric adjustment knob, eyecup, viewfinder eyepiece, MENU, INFO, JUMP, playback, erase, LCD monitor, setting button, tripod socket, access lamp, quick control dial, multi-controller, AE lock/FE lock, AF point selection, strap mount, CF card slot cover, battery compartment cover, and battery compartment cover release lever.

LCD panel information diagram labeling shutter speed, busy status, ISO speed, white balance icons, drive mode, AF mode, metering mode, shots remaining, aperture, battery check, flash exposure compensation, and CF card warning status.

Viewfinder information diagram showing focusing screen, partial metering circle, AF points, AE lock/FE lock, focus confirmation light, max burst, white balance correction, exposure level indicator, shutter speed, aperture, ISO speed, flash-ready indicator, high-speed sync, flash exposure compensation, and CF card warning.
Camera mode dial diagram with Creative Zone modes A-DEP, M, Av, Tv, and P, a Full Auto mark, and Image Zone/Basic Zone scene icons.
Battery Charger CG-580 drawing with labels for battery pack slot, red lamp, and power plug.
Battery Charger CB-5L drawing with a power cord, battery pack slot, red lamp, and power cord socket labeled.
A small icon of the camera power switch with ON and OFF labels.
A small icon showing the main dial as a half gear or ridged wheel symbol.
A small icon showing the quick control dial as a circular ridged wheel.
A small multi-controller icon showing a central dot with arrows in eight directions.
A small SET button icon showing the word SET inside a circle.
Strap attachment diagram on a Canon camera. Numbered arrows show threading the strap through the strap mount and buckle, looping it through, and pulling it tight.
Close-up of a Canon strap or strap buckle on a camera strap, with a callout line pointing to the buckle area.
Battery charger illustration showing the battery compartment cover or protective cover being lifted open with an arrow.
Battery pack placed into the charger, with an arrow and a double-headed mark showing alignment of the battery and charger contacts.
Two-panel charger plug illustration showing the built-in power plug folded out and the charger plugged into a wall outlet.
Charger power cord connection diagram showing a cord plugged into the charger and the wall outlet, with arrows labeled 1 and 2.
Recharge level table for the red lamp: 0-50% blinks once per second, 50-75% blinks twice per second, 75-90% blinks three times per second, and 90% or higher lights on.
Battery compartment cover closing or battery insertion diagram with a small battery icon and an arrow showing the cover moving closed.
Camera battery compartment opening step. Arrows labeled 1 and 2 show sliding the release and opening the battery compartment cover on the camera bottom.
Battery insertion step 2. A battery pack is lowered into the open camera battery compartment with a large downward arrow.
Battery compartment closing step 3. A large curved arrow shows closing the compartment cover on the camera bottom.
LCD monitor battery check screen. A battery icon near the lower left is circled, and the display includes AWB and other shooting status boxes.
Battery level legend with three battery icons: Battery level OK, Battery level is low, and Battery must be recharged.

Battery life table with temperatures and shooting conditions. At 20 degrees C / 68 degrees F it shows approx. 1000 shots with no flash and approx. 700 with 50% flash use; at 0 degrees C / 32 degrees F it shows approx. 750 and approx. 550.
Battery removal step 1. The camera battery compartment cover is opened by sliding a latch and lifting the cover, marked with arrows 1 and 2.
Battery removal step 2. The battery release lever is moved and the battery rises out of the open compartment, with arrows labeled 1 and 2.
DC coupler connection step showing a Canon AC adapter or coupler connected to a cable, with an arrow pointing into the socket.
Power cord connection step showing the adapter cord plugged into the wall and the DC coupler or adapter, with arrows labeled 1 and 2.
Camera battery compartment diagram showing a cord placed through a groove while the compartment cover is partly open.
DC coupler insertion diagram showing the coupler or dummy battery inserted into the camera battery compartment and the cable routed out through the cord groove.
Lens mounting preparation diagram with two panels showing removal of the rear lens cap and body cap from a Canon lens and camera body.
Lens mounting diagram showing the lens alignment mark matched to the camera mount mark, then the lens rotated into place with a curved arrow.
Close-up of a lens focus mode switch labeled AF and MF, with the switch set to AF and the lens mounted on the camera.
Lens detaching diagram showing pressing the lens release button and turning the lens in the direction of the arrows before pulling it away.
CF card cover opening diagram on the side of the camera, with arrows showing sliding and opening the card slot cover.
CF card insertion diagram showing a CompactFlash card aligned with the open card slot and inserted into the camera.
CF card cover closing diagram showing the side cover being closed and slid until it locks, with arrows labeled 1 and 2.
Camera LCD panel crop showing shooting status symbols. Readable items include AWB and a shots-remaining value of 75.
Camera side view showing the card-slot cover being opened or closed with numbered arrows 1 and 2. The access lamp is labeled below the card door.
Camera card compartment diagram showing a CF card being ejected from the open side cover. Large arrows and step number 2 indicate pressing the eject button and pulling the card out.
Top camera control diagram showing the power switch beside ON and OFF labels. A curved arrow points the switch toward ON, and a trash can icon is visible nearby.
Camera shutter button diagram showing a finger pressing the shutter halfway. A downward arrow points to the shutter button on the camera top.
Camera shutter button diagram showing a finger pressing the shutter completely. A downward arrow points farther into the shutter button on the camera top.
Camera top controls diagram showing a finger pressing a button near the LCD panel while a large arrow indicates turning the main dial by the lens.
Camera top controls diagram showing the main dial near the shutter button being turned, with a curved arrow over the dial.
Camera rear and top diagram showing a button press and the rear Quick Control Dial being turned, with arrows over both controls.
Rear camera diagram showing the Quick Control Dial around the SET button being turned, with a large curved arrow.
Camera control diagram showing the multi-controller joystick. Arrows indicate movement in multiple directions and a push action.

Menu operations diagram labeling LCD Monitor, MENU button, JUMP button, Quick Control Dial, SET button, menu category color code, menu category, menu items, and menu settings. The sample Quality menu lists Red-eye On/Off, Beep, Shoot without card, AEB, WB SHIFT/BKT, and Custom WB.
Table of menu category icons and meanings. Red is Shooting menu for shooting-related menu, blue is Playback menu for image playback-related menu, and yellow is Set-up menu for camera basic settings.
Vertical sequence of five camera menu screenshots showing navigation through tabs and highlighted menu items, ending with Shoot without card set to Off.
Dense menu settings table for a camera. It lists shooting, playback, and set-up menu items with options and page numbers; many small entries are visible but not all are readable in detail.
Camera setup menu screenshot with Clear settings highlighted. Nearby items include Video system NTSC, Communication Normal, Format, Sensor clean., and Firmware Ver. 1.0.0.
Confirmation dialog titled Clear all camera settings. The message repeats Clear all camera settings, with Cancel and OK buttons; OK is highlighted.

Default camera settings table. It lists AF mode One-Shot AF, AF point selection Automatic AF point selection, metering Evaluative, drive Single shooting, exposure compensation 0, AEB Off, flash exposure compensation 0, Quality L, ISO speed 100, color space sRGB, white balance AWB, color temperature 5200K, WB correction Off, WB-BKT amount Off, and Parameters Parameter 2.

Camera setup menu screenshot with Language highlighted and set to English. Nearby visible items include Date/Time, File numbering Continuous, Video system NTSC, Communication Normal, Format, and Custom Functions.
Language selection menu with English highlighted. Other visible choices include Deutsch, Francais, Nederlands, Dansk, Suomi, Italiano, Norsk, Svenska, Espanol, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese.

Language table mapping camera language names to English names: English, Deutsch/German, Francais/French, Nederlands/Dutch, Dansk/Danish, Suomi/Finnish, Italiano/Italian, Norsk/Norwegian, Svenska/Swedish, Espanol/Spanish, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese.
Set-up menu screenshot showing Auto Play, Review time, Auto power off, Auto rotate, LCD Brightness, Date/Time, and File numbering. A side list marks step numbers 1 and 2 beside the menu.

Set-up menu screenshot with Date/Time highlighted. Visible settings include Review time 2 sec., Auto power off 1 min., Auto rotate On, LCD Brightness slider, Date/Time 08/18/04 13:24, File numbering Continuous, and Language English.
Date/Time setting screen showing date 08.18.2004 and time 13:24 with format mm/dd/yy. Up and down arrows indicate changing the selected date field, with SET and MENU icons at the bottom.
Date/Time setting screen focused on the date-format field. It shows 08.18.2004, time 13:24, the highlighted format mm/dd/yy, and SET and MENU icons at the bottom.
Camera battery compartment diagram showing the cover open and numbered arrows 1, 2, and 3 for removing the date/time battery holder.
Camera battery compartment diagram showing the date/time battery holder lifted out of the open battery compartment.
Camera battery holder diagram with small rays around the installed coin cell, indicating the battery orientation or placement in the holder.
Camera battery compartment diagram showing the date/time battery holder being inserted back into the compartment, with arrows labeled 1 and 2.
Camera setup menu screenshot with Sensor clean. highlighted. Nearby items include Video system NTSC, Communication Normal, Format, Custom Functions, Clear settings, and Firmware Ver. 1.0.0.
Sensor clean confirmation dialog. It says Turn off the camera after sensor cleaning and shows Cancel and OK buttons, with OK highlighted.
Camera sensor cleaning diagram showing a blower aimed into the open lens mount while the mirror or shutter area is exposed.
Camera viewfinder adjustment diagram showing the dioptric adjustment knob being turned left or right. An inset shows minus and plus marks around the knob.
Illustration of proper camera holding positions. It shows horizontal shooting and vertical shooting postures, plus an inset of foot placement.
Camera mode dial diagram with a large arrow labeled Basic zone. The dial shows icons and letters including A-DEP, M, Av, Tv, P, and automatic/basic-zone symbols.
Close-up of camera mode dial showing the fully automatic rectangle icon aligned with the index mark.
Camera shutter button diagram labeled step 3, showing a finger pressing the shutter button to focus the subject.
Camera LCD and viewfinder information diagram. It shows focus and exposure indicators including AWB, a value 125, 11, shots remaining 75, a battery icon, and AI FOCUS.
Camera rear diagram labeled step 5, showing the shutter being pressed and a captured portrait displayed on the LCD monitor.
Sample portrait photograph of a smiling person, used as an example image for portrait shooting.
Sample black-and-white landscape photo of a boat on water with mountains and clouds in the background.
Sample close-up photo of a sunflower or large flower in front of buildings, illustrating close-up shooting.
Sample sports photo of a surfer riding a wave, illustrating action shooting.
Sample night portrait photo of a woman with city lights in the background.
Sample indoor room photo with curtains, table, and ceiling light, illustrating flash-off shooting.

Camera operation diagram with numbered steps. The top view shows a finger pressing the shutter button halfway near the lens, and the lower view shows an LCD panel with ISO 100 and an autofocus or focus confirmation area.
Camera top-view diagram showing a finger pressing the shutter button fully, with a flash or indicator mark near the hot shoe and step number 4.

Two camera menu screenshots for image quality. The first menu highlights Quality above Red-eye On/Off, Beep, and Shoot w/o card. The second screen lists image-recording quality choices including large, medium, small, RAW plus JPEG combinations, and RAW.

Image-recording quality table with columns Image-recording quality, File Format extension, Pixels, and Print Size. It lists Large Fine and Large Normal JPEG at 3504 x 2336, Medium Fine and Medium Normal JPEG at 2544 x 1696, Small Fine and Small Normal JPEG at 1728 x 1152, and RAW at 3504 x 2336 CR2.

Image quality capacity table with columns Image-recording quality, Image File Size approximate MB, and Possible Shots. Values include Large Fine 3.6 MB 66 shots, Large Normal 1.8 MB 133 shots, Medium Fine 2.2 MB 112 shots, Medium Normal 1.1 MB 221 shots, Small Fine 1.2 MB 195 shots, Small Normal 0.6 MB 380 shots, RAW combinations around 18 to 25 shots, and RAW 8.7 MB 27 shots.

Max burst table for continuous shooting. Image-recording qualities are shown across the top, including Large, Medium, Small, RAW, and RAW plus JPEG. Max Burst values include 20, 32, 28, 61, 64, 123, and 6 for RAW modes.
Two-step camera diagram for ISO speed. Step 1 shows pressing a top button near the lens. Step 2 shows the LCD panel displaying ISO 400 while the main dial is turned.
White balance setting diagram. Step 1 shows pressing the AF-WB button on the camera top. Step 2 shows the rear dial and LCD panel, with a daylight sun icon and ONE SHOT text visible.

White balance table with columns Display, Mode, and Color temperature approximate K. It lists AWB Auto 3000-7000, Daylight 5200, Shade 7000, Cloudy twilight sunset 6000, Tungsten 3200, White fluorescent light 4000, Flash 6000, Custom 2000-10000, and Color temperature 2800-10000.
Two-step custom white balance diagram. Step 1 shows pressing a top camera button; step 2 shows a custom white balance icon on the LCD or status display.
Viewfinder diagram for partial metering. A central circle and small autofocus points appear inside the frame, labeled Partial metering, with step number 3.
Camera menu screenshot with Custom WB highlighted. Other visible rows include Beep On, Shoot w/o card On, AEB scale, WB SHIFT/BKT 0,0/+0, Color temp. 5200 K, and Color space sRGB.
Camera LCD image selection screen. The top says Select an image with file number 102-0218, and the bottom shows 1/125, 5.6, 33/33, image quality Large, MENU, and a return icon.
Two-step color temperature diagram. Step 1 shows pressing a camera top button; step 2 shows a K icon on the LCD or status display.
Camera menu screenshot with Color temp. highlighted and set to 5200 K. Other rows include Shoot w/o card On, AEB scale, WB SHIFT/BKT 0,0/+0, Custom WB, Color space sRGB, and Parameters Parameter 2.

Camera menu screenshot with WB SHIFT/BKT highlighted and set to 0,0/+0. Other visible rows include Shoot w/o card On, AEB scale, Custom WB, Color temp. 5200 K, Color space sRGB, and Parameters Parameter 2.
Rear camera control diagram showing arrows in eight directions around the SET button, indicating directional adjustment with the rear controller.
White balance shift and bracketing screen. A grid is labeled G at top, B at left, A at right, and M at bottom, with SHIFT and BKT indicators, numeric fields A2 and G1, BKT plus/minus 0, and SET OK.
Menu screenshot again highlighting WB SHIFT/BKT at 0,0/+0 with the AEB scale above and settings for Custom WB, Color temp. 5200 K, Color space sRGB, and Parameters Parameter 2 below.
Rear camera diagram showing the large dial being turned clockwise beside the SET button and power switch, with step number 3.
White balance bracketing screen with a grid labeled G, B, A, and M. Three dots are spread horizontally, and the BKT field is circled with BA plus/minus 3, indicating blue/amber bias bracketing.
White balance bracketing screen with three dots arranged vertically. The BKT field is circled with MG plus/minus 3, indicating magenta/green bias bracketing.
White balance shift/bracketing screen with a single dot centered on the grid and the BKT field showing plus/minus 0, indicating bracketing canceled.

Color space menu screenshot. The Color space row is highlighted and a small selection box shows sRGB selected above Adobe RGB. Other menu rows include AEB, WB SHIFT/BKT, Custom WB, Color temp., Parameters, and Protect.

Two menu screenshots for selecting processing parameters. The first highlights Parameters set to Parameter 2; the second shows a Parameters screen with Parameter 1 circled and slider rows for Contrast, Sharpness, Saturation, and Color tone.

Processing parameter table with columns Parameter and Description. Rows describe Parameter 1 as vivid and sharp, Parameter 2 as more subdued and natural, Set 1/2/3 as registerable settings for contrast, sharpness, saturation, and color tone, and B/W as black-and-white images.
Camera menu screenshot with Parameters highlighted and set to Parameter 2. Other visible rows include WB SHIFT/BKT, Custom WB, Color temp. 5200 K, Color space sRGB, Protect, and Rotate.
Parameters setting screen with Set 1 circled at the top right. Slider rows are shown for Contrast, Sharpness, Saturation, and Color tone, with MENU at the lower right.
Parameters screen for Set 1 with Sharpness highlighted. Slider rows show Contrast, Sharpness, Saturation, and Color tone, with scale marks and MENU at the lower right.

Parameter effect table with columns Parameter, Minus, and Plus. It lists Contrast low contrast to high contrast, Sharpness less sharp outline to sharp outline, Saturation low saturation to high saturation, and Color tone reddish skin tone to yellowish skin tone.
Parameters screen for Set 1 with Sharpness selected and the adjustment marker shifted toward the plus side of the slider.

Two black-and-white parameter screenshots. The upper screen has B/W selected and shows Contrast, Sharpness, Filter effects N:None, and Toning Effect N:None; the lower screen highlights Sharpness on a similar B/W parameter list.
Black-and-white Parameters screen with Sharpness highlighted and adjusted on a slider. Filter effects and Toning Effect both show N:None, with MENU at the lower right.

title: Camera shutter button: no user removal procedure; half-press and full-press operation

pic_descriptions.description: Camera shutter button diagram showing a finger pressing the shutter halfway. A downward arrow points to the shutter button on the camera top.
Camera shutter button diagram showing a finger pressing the shutter completely. A downward arrow points farther into the shutter button on the camera top.

text:
The camera manual does not provide a user procedure for removing the shutter button. It treats the shutter button as a fixed shooting control. The shutter button has two steps: press it halfway to activate autofocusing (AF) and automatic exposure (AE), then press it completely to release the shutter and take the picture. The camera care section also warns that the camera contains precision electronic circuitry and users should never attempt to disassemble it themselves.

title: Using the camera eyepiece cover before taking photos

pic_descriptions.description: Rear camera drawing showing the eyecup around the viewfinder being removed upward with two arrows.
Rear camera drawing showing an eyepiece cover attached over the viewfinder on the camera strap; a downward arrow points to the cover.

text:
Use the eyepiece cover during self-timer or optional remote switch operation when your eye does not cover the viewfinder eyepiece. Stray light may enter the eyepiece and affect exposure. To attach the cover, remove the eyecup by pushing it upward from the bottom, then slide the eyepiece cover down into the eyepiece groove.
